title: What happens if you leave a phone in a hot car?

lines.text: Leaving your smartphone sitting on a car dashboard on a sunny day can permanently destroy it in minutes.
lines.caps: Never leave your *phone | in a *hot car!

lines.text: On an eighty-degree afternoon, the inside of a closed vehicle can easily spike past one hundred and forty degrees.
lines.caps: Car interiors reach | over *140 degrees | in *minutes

lines.text: Inside your phone, the lithium-ion battery operates with volatile liquid electrolytes.
Extreme heat causes the battery's internal separator film to degrade, triggering thermal runaway.
The battery can swell up like a balloon, cracking the screen glass and risking a chemical fire.
lines.caps: The battery can *swell | and shatter the *glass!

lines.text: Even if it doesn't catch fire, permanent battery capacity drops by over twenty percent after one afternoon.
lines.caps: Loses 20% of its *capacity | in just *one day

lines.text: Always keep your phone in your pocket or out of direct sunlight.
lines.caps: Keep your device in the *shade | to stay *safe!
